added_lemmas.statement:
Consider a directed summary causal graph \(H\) obtained from an acyclic full-time causal graph of a dynamic structural causal model with maximal lag bounded by \(L\), causal sufficiency, and consistency throughout time.  For the singleton query \(P(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))\), if \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) holds, then the effect equals \(P(Y_0=y)\) when \(X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\); when \(X\in\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\), the set \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L,X)\) is a valid adjustment set and
\[
 P(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =\sum_a P(Y_0=y\mid X_{-\gamma}=x,
 \mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}=a)
 P(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}=a).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 2, equation (2), and Lemmas 5.1--5.3 in Section 5.1 of arXiv:2310.14691v5

attestation.note: Checked against the source-of-record arXiv HTML for Theorem 2, equation (2), and Lemmas 5.1--5.3; the node specializes the two published cases and preserves every listed obstruction.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\mathcal A\).  If \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) holds, then \(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) is well defined and, for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\),
\[
 F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x)=\theta_M(y;x).
\]
This conclusion includes eligible cyclic or self-looped directed summaries; it does not assert that the published sufficient graphical condition is necessary.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), and let \(R\in\mathfrak R(H,L)\) be its refinement.  We first verify that \(M\) lies in the class to which \(\mathrm{lem:assaad\text{-}scg\text{-}adjustment}\) applies.

Every directed edge of \(R\) has the form \(i_{t-\ell}\to j_t\) with \(0\le\ell\le L\), by \(\mathrm{ass:refinement\text{-}span}\).  If a directed cycle existed in the full-time graph, the sum of its nonnegative time increments would be zero.  Every edge on that cycle would therefore have lag zero, contradicting \(\mathrm{ass:instantaneous\text{-}acyclicity}\).  Hence the full-time directed graph is acyclic.

The predicate \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\) includes
\(E_{\leftrightarrow}(H)=\varnothing\).  Suppose an exogenous root of \(M\) had two distinct observed children.  By \(\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian}\), that shared root would induce a bidirected edge between those two temporal vertices of \(R\); by \(\mathrm{ass:exact\text{-}summary}\), its coordinate pair would induce a bidirected edge, including a bidirected self-loop when the coordinates agree, in \(H\).  This contradicts \(E_{\leftrightarrow}(H)=\varnothing\).  Thus every exogenous root is private to one observed vertex and the full-time model is causally sufficient.

By the definition of a stationary refinement, translation of time preserves every directed relation in \(R\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:time\text{-}homogeneous}\), the translated structural equation is the same equation after relabelling its shifted arguments.  These two facts give the source's consistency-through-time setup.  The lag bound is \(L\), and \(\mathrm{ass:exact\text{-}summary}\) gives exactly the directed SCG \(H^{\to}\).  Consequently
\[
 M\in\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ours}}(H,L,\mathcal A)
 \subseteq \mathscr C_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L),
\]
where the right-hand side denotes the causally sufficient, time-consistent dynamic-SCM class in the cited result.  This is a class inclusion, not an identification assumption.

There are two cases.  If
\(X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\), the first conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem:assaad\text{-}scg\text{-}adjustment}\) yields
\[
 \theta_M(y;x)=P_M(Y_0=y)
 =F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x).
\]
If \(X\in\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\), the predicate
\(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\) says exactly that neither listed obstruction holds.  The second conclusion of the cited lemma therefore gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \theta_M(y;x)
 &=\sum_{a\in\mathfrak a_{\gamma}}
 P_M\bigl(Y_0=y\mid X_{-\gamma}=x,
 \mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}=a\bigr)
 P_M\bigl(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}=a\bigr)\\
 &=F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x),
 \end{split}
\]
where the second equality expands each conditional probability as the cylinder ratio in \(\mathrm{def:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}certificate}\).

It remains to check typing and support.  The set
\(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\) contains at most \(n(L+1)\) temporal vertices, so \(\mathfrak a_{\gamma}\) is finite by \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}alphabet}\).  For every \(a\in\mathfrak a_{\gamma}\), \(\mathrm{ass:cylinder\text{-}positivity}\) gives
\[
 P_M\bigl(C_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\cup
 \{(X,-\gamma)\},(a,x))\bigr)>0.
\]
Thus every displayed division is defined.  All numerator, denominator, and marginal terms are probabilities of finite cylinders in the common space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\); the expression uses only a finite sum, products, and ratios with positive denominators.  By \(\mathrm{def:cylinder\text{-}language}\),
\(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\).  Since \(M\) was arbitrary, the equality holds uniformly over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).
added_lemmas.justification: This proposition proves that the published causally sufficient SCG adjustment rule is a sound finite-cylinder success branch for the present stationary model class.
added_lemmas.gap: The result imports and transfers Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui's sufficient coverage; it is not claimed as a new identification criterion or as a complete cyclic rule.
added_lemmas.consumer: It lets EasyRCA certify eligible cyclic and self-looped causally sufficient lag queries that the acyclic fallback would otherwise leave unknown.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Define \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) by the following ordered finite rules.  First, if the input is exactly \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), return \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\).  Second, if the input is the binary lag-switch query of \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\) with \(x=0\) and \(y=1\), return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A))\), where the certificate consists of the two displayed rational structural tables and their rational noise laws.  Third, compute the finite-graph predicate \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) from \(\mathrm{def:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}certificate}\).  If it holds, construct the finite set \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L,X)\) and return \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\), using the marginal branch of \(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\) when \(X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\) and its displayed adjustment branch otherwise.  Fourth, if the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, construct \(G^\star\), restrict it to \(A^\star=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})\), and run memoized ordinary ID on \(G^\star[A^\star]\); return \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\) if ID returns \(F\), and return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) if ID fails.  In every other case return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).  The ancestry, descendant, simple-path, and directed-cycle tests in the third rule are finite graph searches on \(H\).  Count initialization and each ordered top-level rule evaluation as one transition.  An ID memo state labels each vertex of \(A^\star\) as absent, random, or fixed, and repeated states are not revisited.  Set
\[
 B_\star(n,L,\gamma)=5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}.
\]

proposed.name: Published causally sufficient SCG adjustment certificate
proposed.construction:
Write \(H^{\to}=(V,E_{\to}(H))\), and let directed ancestors and descendants include the vertex itself.  For a directed graph \(G\), let \(\operatorname{Cyc}(v;G)\) be the set of simple directed cycles through \(v\), including a self-loop, and let \(\operatorname{Cyc}_{>1}(v;G)\) retain only cycles containing at least two distinct vertices.  Let \(\mathcal B_{\sigma}(X,Y;H^{\to})\) be the set of paths \(\pi=(v_1=X,\ldots,v_m=Y)\), \(m\ge 2\), with distinct vertices, consecutive vertices adjacent in \(H^{\to}\), first edge \(v_2\to X\), and no internal collider \(v_{j-1}\to v_j\leftarrow v_{j+1}\).  Thus these are exactly the \(\sigma\)-active back-door paths given the empty set in the directed summary convention of Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--G\"ossler--Meynaoui.  Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathsf O_1(H,X,Y,\gamma)
 &:=\bigl[\gamma\ne0\ \wedge\
 \operatorname{Cyc}_{>1}(X;H^{\to}\setminus\{Y\})\ne\varnothing\bigr],\\
 \mathsf O_2(H,X,Y,\gamma)
 &:=\Bigl[\exists\pi=(v_1=X,\ldots,v_m=Y)\in
 \mathcal B_{\sigma}(X,Y;H^{\to}):
 \{v_2,\ldots,v_{m-1}\}\subseteq
 \operatorname{Desc}_{H^{\to}}(X),\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\bigl(m>2\bigr)\ \vee\
 \bigl(m=2\wedge\gamma\ne1\bigr)\ \vee\
 \bigl(m=2\wedge\gamma=1\wedge
 \operatorname{Cyc}(Y;H^{\to}\setminus\{X\})\ne\varnothing\bigr)
 \Bigr],
 \end{split}
\]
and
\[
 \mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)
 :=[E_{\leftrightarrow}(H)=\varnothing]\wedge
 \Bigl[X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\ \vee\
 \bigl(X\in\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\wedge
 \neg\mathsf O_1(H,X,Y,\gamma)\wedge
 \neg\mathsf O_2(H,X,Y,\gamma)\bigr)\Bigr].
\]
Put \(D_X=\operatorname{Desc}_{H^{\to}}(X)\) and define the finite temporal adjustment set
\[
 \mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L,X)
 =\{Z_{-\gamma-\ell}:Z\in D_X,\ 1\le\ell\le L\}
 \cup
 \{Z_{-\gamma-\ell}:Z\in V\setminus D_X,\ 0\le\ell\le L\}.
\]
For a law \(P\) on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), let
\(\mathfrak a_{\gamma}=\prod_{Z_s\in\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}}\mathcal A_Z\), and define
\[
 F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P;y,x)=
 \begin{cases}
 P\bigl(C_{\mathcal A}(\{(Y,0)\},y)\bigr),
 &X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y),\\[1mm]
 \displaystyle
 \sum_{a\in\mathfrak a_{\gamma}}
 \frac{P\bigl(C_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\cup
 \{(X,-\gamma),(Y,0)\},(a,x,y))\bigr)
 P\bigl(C_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}},a)\bigr)}
 {P\bigl(C_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\cup
 \{(X,-\gamma)\},(a,x))\bigr)},
 &X\in\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y).
 \end{cases}
\]
The empty-cylinder convention is
\(C_{\mathcal A}(\varnothing,\varnothing)=\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives sufficient summary-graph front-door conditions and a common do-free expression for selected micro total effects under latent confounding.
The ID algorithm returns an observational functional or a hedge and is complete for a fixed finite ADMG.
Theorem 1.1 bounds the graph segment needed to decide identification for one fully specified periodic latent-confounded time-series graph.
A possible-c-component and region recursion is sound and complete for causal identification over the finite graph class represented by a PAG.
Fixing kernels and intrinsic sets characterize identifiable effects and nested constraints in a fixed ADMG.
Do-calculus is sound and complete for macro total effects in latent-confounded summary causal graphs.
A complete graphical characterization and two finite adjustment sets identify linear direct effects from summary causal graphs under no hidden confounding.
Under causal sufficiency, Theorem 2 gives sufficient summary-graph conditions and a finite adjustment set for singleton lag-specific total effects.
Necessary and sufficient conditions and a pseudo-linear algorithm characterize identification by common adjustment in causally sufficient summary graphs.
Graphical fixing outputs can be compiled into weight-based and influence-function estimators under independent sampling.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The 2024 causally sufficient SCG result is now explicitly imported and matched by a proved class-inclusion transfer, while the remaining comparator positions are unchanged.

prose_updates.tldr: The full sound-and-complete lag-robust fixing theorem remains open, but the terminating three-way certified procedure now has a broader sound success region. In addition to the concrete outside-front-door witness and successful saturated ordinary-ID calls for acyclic loop-free directed summaries, it imports Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui's 2024 causally sufficient SCG criterion: when \(H\) has no bidirected edge, the procedure returns the marginal for the no-ancestor case or their explicit finite adjustment functional when neither listed cyclic or back-door obstruction holds. This branch covers eligible cyclic and self-looped summaries and is established by an explicit inclusion of the present stationary semi-Markovian class in the published causally sufficient setup. The verified binary lag-switch pair remains a direct failure certificate, and all other undecided inputs return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). The revised transition bound is \(5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}\). Every success supports the existing cylinder plug-in and HAC delta-method inference under the stated positivity, mixing, bandwidth, and variance conditions.

project_justification.gap: Published causally sufficient SCG adjustment criteria do cover a substantial cyclic and self-looped subclass, but they do not address latent-confounded summaries or supply a sound-and-complete lag-specific micro-effect decision rule over the present fixed-alphabet stationary refinement class. Fixed-graph hedges likewise do not automatically preserve time homogeneity, exact summary, positivity, equality of the entire process law, and unchanged coordinate alphabets under a refinement switch.
project_justification.niche: The attainable contribution is certified partial identification with graph-native abstention. The procedure can faithfully incorporate the published causally sufficient adjustment region, add saturated-ID successes under latent confounding for acyclic loop-free directed summaries, and exhibit a direct cyclic lag-switch nonidentification pair even though each refinement is individually identifiable. The remaining latent-confounded cyclic cases require the still-open offset-sensitive normal form and direct fixed-alphabet witness construction.
project_justification.fill: The ordered procedure recognizes one proved outside-front-door success, one proved positive stationary lag-switch failure, the explicit Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui adjustment branch whenever its finite SCG predicate holds, and otherwise a memoized ordinary-ID call on at most \(n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\) ancestral roles when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free. It returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) whenever these certified rules do not decide the query. This yields sound finite-cylinder successes for additional cyclic and self-looped causally sufficient summaries while preserving the honest absence of a completeness claim.

prose_updates.related_work: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui give sufficient graphical conditions and finite adjustment sets for singleton total effects from directed SCGs under causal sufficiency and consistency throughout time. The present procedure imports that coverage explicitly rather than claiming it as novelty: exact summary and translation invariance provide the SCG relation, time-homogeneous equations provide consistency through time, and the absence of bidirected summary edges together with independent semi-Markovian roots yields causal sufficiency. Assaad's later micro front-door result treats selected latent-confounded effects, Ferreira and Assaad treat macro effects and linear direct effects, and Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier characterize common adjustment under causal sufficiency. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman bound identification for one specified periodic fine graph; Jaber and coauthors decide a finite graph class represented by one PAG; Shpitser and Pearl establish ID for one finite ADMG; and Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser develop fixed-ADMG fixing. None supplies the missing direct fixed-alphabet stationary rejection construction or complete offset-sensitive cross-refinement calculus for latent-confounded cyclic SCGs. The note's new claims therefore remain the stationary transfer, certified combination, and explicit lag-switch obstruction, not the imported adjustment criterion itself.
prose_updates.interpretation: A success tag is a positive causal certificate. It may now arise from the concrete outside-front-door rule, the imported causally sufficient SCG adjustment rule, or a successful saturated ordinary-ID call; in every case the returned finite-cylinder arithmetic functional equals the lag-specific intervention probability in every compatible SCM. A failure tag remains a negative certificate consisting of two fixed-alphabet stationary SCMs with the same entire observational process law and different target values. An unknown tag is neither and records that the current sound rules do not decide the query. EasyRCA ranks only successful queries and does not turn either failure or unresolved status into a low transmission score.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The added adjustment branch does not address the core latent-confounded cyclic obstruction because it requires the bidirected summary edge set to be empty. In the unresolved region, a finite rejection witness may contain several temporal roles of the same observed coordinate; independent-shift replication then attempts to place several role values into one coordinate-time variable, while product-slot repairs enlarge the fixed alphabet. The procedure avoids that defect by constructing its only general failure example directly and returning unknown elsewhere. Strict stationarity and bounded structural lag also do not make the observed process finite-order Markov, so transition-kernel truncation and semantic gluing of refinement-specific formulas still cannot supply completeness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves sound partial certification, not a sound-and-complete TID-SCG dichotomy. The Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui branch is imported published coverage under causal sufficiency and only for the paper's stated sufficient graphical condition; no necessity or novelty is claimed for that criterion. The acyclic saturated-ID branch is sound but not claimed complete for uniform identification, the static boundary still returns unknown on ID failure, the front-door result remains the concrete outside-family witness, and the direct failure branch covers the verified binary lag-switch query. Latent-confounded cyclic cases outside these rules remain open. The HAC theorem applies only after a sound success and additionally requires cylinder positivity, geometric beta mixing, the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).

statement_notes.justification: This is the explicit class-inclusion proof that makes the published adjustment result a sound branch of the local procedure.
